title: chain definition
description: An ordered multi-skill playbook, for bin/chain.py. A chain records the sequence and where a run got to; it never invokes a skill. Project chains live in .design-suite/chains/ and take precedence over the suite's templates/chains/.

id.description: Stable identifier used to record this step's outcome. Renaming one loses that step's recorded position.

skill.description: Skill to run, without the leading slash.

args.description: Arguments to pass, if the skill takes them.

purpose.description: What this step is for, in one line. Shown when the step comes up.

decisionPoint.description: What to ask the user before running this step. Shown before the step runs, not after.

skipIf.description: The condition under which this step should be skipped. Prose, evaluated by a human — a chain runner that decided this for itself would be guessing at project state.

checkpoint.description: Whether the chain stops for explicit sign-off after this step. DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Set false only when the step has no confirmation requirement of its own and nothing downstream depends on a human having looked at its output.

checkpointReason.description: Why this step is (or is not) a checkpoint. Required reading for anyone tempted to turn one off.

onFail.description: What happens if the step does not succeed. `halt` stops the chain; `skip` moves on. Defaults to halt — a chain that continues past a failed step produces work built on a step that did not happen.
